_readme: profile.example.json — the Merchandise Returns Engine identity profile (Blueprint M32).
Copy this file to 'profile.json', replace every value with YOUR OWN, and the engine runs
under your identity with zero code edits. The values below are a FICTIONAL example user.
Where the engine looks for your profile, first hit wins:
1. an explicit --config / path argument passed to the loader
4. /opt/data/mer_profile.json  (the VPS default — a default, never an assumption)
Keys beginning with an underscore are documentation and are ignored by the loader.
NEVER put a password, OAuth token or API key in this file. 'google_token_file' is a PATH
to the credential file, not the credential.

_fields.legal_name: REQUIRED. Your full legal name exactly as it should appear on a demand letter and on a small-claims petition. Every outbound letter is signed with this.
_fields.email: REQUIRED. The mailbox the engine sends from and reads replies in. Must be the mailbox you OAuth-connected. Test-mode sends are redirected here.
_fields.phone: Optional. E.164 format preferred. Used for the voice-escalation nag and printed on statutory demand letters. Omit or leave empty to disable voice escalation.
_fields.mailing_address: Optional but strongly recommended. Your postal address, used on statutory pre-suit demand letters (many states require a mailable address). A string with newlines, or an array of lines.
_fields.state: REQUIRED — NEVER DEFAULTED. Full state name, e.g. 'Ohio'. Decides your state Attorney General, your BBB region, your deceptive-trade-practices statute and your damages cap. The engine refuses to run without it rather than guess.
_fields.county: REQUIRED — NEVER DEFAULTED. Your county of residence, without the word 'County'. Decides the small-claims / justice-court venue where a petition would actually be filed.
_fields.multica_workspace_id: REQUIRED. The UUID of YOUR Multica workspace — the system of record for your cases. Find it with: multica workspace list --output json
_fields.multica_project_id: Optional. UUID of a project inside that workspace to scope cases to. null = the whole workspace.
_fields.notify: Optional. How the engine pings you. {'channel': 'telegram', 'telegram_chat_id': '<your numeric chat id>'} or {'channel': 'none'} for no push notifications. The chat id is not a secret; the bot TOKEN is, and lives in .env, never here.
_fields.signature_block: Optional. Exactly how letters are signed, as a string with newlines or an array of lines. When omitted it defaults to your legal_name on one line and your email on the next.
_fields.calendar_id: Optional. Google Calendar id that case deadlines sync to. Defaults to your 'email' when omitted.
_fields.google_token_file: Optional. Filesystem PATH to the OAuth token JSON for your mailbox (never the token itself). Defaults to the VPS path /opt/data/<mailbox>_google_token.json.
_fields.llm_providers: Optional (M36). An ORDERED LIST of OpenAI-compatible chat endpoints the reply classifier tries, top to bottom; when none answers it degrades to the deterministic heuristic and the engine keeps running. Omit this key entirely and you get the shipped default ladder (NanoGPT/GLM then MiniMax-M3) — identical to pre-M36 behavior. Set it to [] if you have no LLM at all; that is a supported, working (degraded) state, not an error. Each entry: {'name': label for logs, 'base_url': REQUIRED e.g. 'https://api.openai.com/v1' ('/chat/completions' is appended), 'model': REQUIRED e.g. 'gpt-4o-mini', 'api_key_env': the NAME of the env var holding your key — never the key itself, null for a keyless local server like Ollama; optional: 'max_tokens' (default 1500), 'reasoning' (default false), 'strip_think' (default true), 'temperature' (default 0), 'timeout' seconds (default 40), 'extra' object merged into the request body}. REASONING MODELS: set 'reasoning': true for a model that emits a <think> block before its answer (MiniMax-M3 does) — it floors max_tokens at 1500, which is the fix for the truncation bug where the whole answer was spent on reasoning. 'strip_think' removes that block before parsing and is ON for every provider by default. A provider whose api_key_env is not set is SKIPPED, so you can list several and only the ones you have keys for are used. $MER_LLM_PROVIDERS (inline JSON, a file path, or 'none') overrides this key; see scripts/vps/README.md -> 'LLM provider configuration'. NEVER put an actual API key here.
